clause_text: Security deposit shall be equal to 2 months' rent and refunded within 15 days of vacating the premises after deducting valid dues.
rationale: Within typical 2-3 month market convention; refund timeline reasonable.

clause_text: Tenant shall pay a security deposit of 3 months' rent, to be returned in full within 30 days of handing over vacant possession, subject to deductions for damages beyond normal wear and tear.
rationale: Standard deposit amount, reasonable refund window, deduction scope limited to genuine damages.

clause_text: Security deposit of 6 months' rent shall be collected and refunded within 45 days of vacating, minus outstanding utility bills.
rationale: 6 months exceeds typical 2-3 month convention; 45-day refund window longer than ideal, though not illegal.

clause_text: Deposit amount equal to 5 months' rent shall be adjusted towards the final two months of tenancy in lieu of a cash refund.
rationale: Adjusting deposit against final rent instead of a proper refund is tenant-disadvantageous and ambiguous on surplus handling.

clause_text: Refund of security deposit shall be processed only after landlord's satisfaction with the condition of the property, without specifying a timeline.
rationale: No defined refund timeline creates room for indefinite withholding; subjective 'satisfaction' standard is vague.

clause_text: Tenant shall pay a security deposit equal to 11 months' rent at the time of signing the agreement.
rationale: Extreme outlier vs 2-3 month market convention; no statutory cap applies but this deviates far beyond normal practice.

clause_text: Security deposit shall not be refunded if the tenant vacates before completion of the lock-in period, irrespective of reason.
rationale: Blanket non-refund clause undermines the basic purpose of a deposit, which should be refundable minus legitimate deductions.

clause_text: Landlord reserves the right to deduct any amount from the security deposit at his sole discretion without providing receipts or justification.
rationale: Unilateral deduction without itemized justification is a recognized unfair contract term regardless of statutory cap.

clause_text: Security deposit collected shall not exceed the limits applicable under the Delhi Rent Control Act, 1958 for tenancies within its scope, and shall be refunded on vacating the premises.
rationale: The DRCA clearly applies only within its statutory scope, but the Act text reviewed does not state a general two-month security-deposit cap. The clause is therefore not labeled as a DRCA deposit-cap rule.

clause_text: Security deposit shall be refunded within 90 days of vacating the premises, subject to landlord's inspection report.
rationale: 90-day refund window is longer than typical reasonable timeframe even for Act-covered tenancies.

clause_text: Either party may terminate the tenancy by providing one month's written notice to the other party.
rationale: Standard, symmetric one-month notice period for both parties.

clause_text: The agreement shall have a lock-in period of 3 months, during which neither party may terminate without mutual consent.
rationale: Short, mutual lock-in period is common and reasonable in the Delhi rental market.

clause_text: Tenant shall provide two months' written notice to vacate, while landlord may terminate the agreement with 15 days' notice.
rationale: Asymmetric notice periods disadvantage the tenant; common in practice but worth flagging as unbalanced.

clause_text: Lock-in period of 12 months shall apply, during which tenant vacating early shall forfeit the entire security deposit.
rationale: Full-term lock-in with full deposit forfeiture is a harsh penalty structure relative to typical 3-6 month lock-ins.

clause_text: Landlord may terminate the tenancy at any time without notice if he deems it necessary.
rationale: No-notice termination at landlord's sole discretion bypasses due process requirements for eviction.

clause_text: Tenant shall not be entitled to any notice period before eviction under any circumstances.
rationale: Blanket waiver of notice rights is not enforceable; eviction requires due legal process regardless of contract wording.

clause_text: Eviction of tenant shall be carried out only through due process before the Rent Controller, on grounds recognized under the Delhi Rent Control Act, 1958.
rationale: Correctly reflects that eviction for Act-covered tenancies requires Rent Controller proceedings on specified grounds.

clause_text: Landlord may change locks or restrict access to the premises if rent is delayed by more than 3 days.
rationale: Self-help eviction (changing locks without a court order) is illegal regardless of rent bracket or delay duration.

clause_text: Lock-in period of 11 months applies with no provision for early exit even in case of job relocation or emergency.
rationale: Full-term lock-in with zero exit flexibility is rigid compared to common market practice allowing negotiated early exit.

clause_text: Tenant may terminate the agreement early by providing 2 months' notice and forfeiting one month's deposit as an early-exit charge.
rationale: Reasonable, clearly defined early-exit mechanism with proportionate charge.

clause_text: Landlord shall be responsible for structural repairs, while tenant shall bear minor day-to-day maintenance costs.
rationale: Standard, balanced allocation of repair responsibility.

clause_text: Major repairs including plumbing and electrical fittings shall be undertaken by the landlord at his own cost.
rationale: Landlord bearing major/structural repair costs is standard practice.

clause_text: Tenant shall bear the cost of all repairs during the tenancy, including structural and major appliance repairs, except in case of natural disaster.
rationale: Shifting structural repair burden onto tenant is an overreach compared to standard practice.

clause_text: Any repair cost incurred by the tenant shall be reimbursed by the landlord only upon prior written approval, without a defined response timeline.
rationale: Lack of a defined approval/reimbursement timeline creates room for indefinite delay.

clause_text: Tenant shall bear full responsibility for all repairs and maintenance, including structural damage, regardless of cause.
rationale: Making tenant liable for structural damage regardless of cause (including landlord's own building defects) is an unreasonable risk transfer.

clause_text: Any deduction from the security deposit for repairs shall be at the landlord's sole discretion without supporting invoices.
rationale: Unsupported unilateral deductions lack the accountability expected in a fair deposit-return process.

clause_text: Society maintenance charges shall be borne by the tenant, while property tax and structural repairs remain the landlord's responsibility.
rationale: Standard, commonly accepted split of recurring vs. structural costs.

clause_text: Tenant shall pay for pest control and appliance servicing on a quarterly basis regardless of actual need.
rationale: Mandatory recurring charges regardless of actual need are an unusual, tenant-unfavorable cost structure.

clause_text: Landlord shall maintain the premises in a habitable condition and undertake essential repairs as required to keep the property fit for occupation.
rationale: Reflects the landlord's general obligation to maintain habitability, consistent with tenant protection intent of the DRCA.

clause_text: Landlord shall not be liable for any repairs during the tenancy under any circumstances, including basic habitability issues like water leakage or electrical faults.
rationale: Blanket waiver of landlord's basic habitability obligations is an extreme and unenforceable risk transfer.

clause_text: Rent shall be increased by not more than 10%, once in three years, with at least 30 days' written notice, as per Delhi Rent Control Act provisions applicable to this tenancy.
rationale: Section 6A permits a ten-per-cent increase every three years, while Section 8 requires written notice and makes the increase recoverable after expiry of 30 days from notice.

clause_text: Rent shall increase by 5% annually with one month's written notice prior to each revision.
rationale: Modest annual escalation with reasonable advance notice; standard market practice.

clause_text: Rent shall increase by 10% annually with 15 days' notice before each revision.
rationale: Shorter notice than the conventional 1-3 month range gives tenant little time to plan around the increase.

clause_text: Rent may be revised annually at landlord's discretion based on prevailing market rates, without a defined percentage cap.
rationale: Open-ended, undefined escalation basis creates unpredictability for the tenant.

clause_text: Landlord may increase rent at any time during the tenancy without prior notice to the tenant.
rationale: No-notice, any-time rent increase during a fixed term contradicts basic contractual fairness and typical practice.

clause_text: Rent shall increase by 25% every six months for the duration of the tenancy.
rationale: 25% biannual escalation is a significant outlier vs. typical 5-10% annual market convention.

clause_text: Rent shall remain fixed for the duration of the 11-month agreement, with revision only upon renewal by mutual consent.
rationale: Fixed-term rent with mutual-consent renewal revision is standard, tenant-favorable practice.

clause_text: Rent shall be increased by 10% every year instead of once in three years as generally applicable under the Delhi Rent Control Act, 1958 for Act-covered tenancies.
rationale: Exceeds the standard revision frequency described in secondary sources for Act-covered tenancies -- verify against primary Section text.

clause_text: Any refusal by tenant to accept a rent increase shall be treated as grounds for immediate eviction without notice.
rationale: Treating rent-increase refusal as automatic eviction grounds bypasses due legal process entirely.

clause_text: Any increase in rent shall be mutually agreed upon in writing and shall not exceed the percentage specified in this agreement.
rationale: Requires mutual written agreement and a defined cap; fair and predictable structure.

clause_text: Either party may terminate this agreement with 30 days' written notice, without assigning any reason.
rationale: Standard, symmetric no-fault termination clause.

clause_text: Tenant shall be evicted only on grounds recognized under Section 14 of the Delhi Rent Control Act, 1958, including non-payment of rent or bona fide requirement by the landlord, subject to Rent Controller's order.
rationale: Correctly reflects statutory eviction grounds and due-process requirement for Act-covered tenancies.

clause_text: Landlord may terminate the agreement without cause upon 15 days' written notice.
rationale: Short 15-day notice for landlord-initiated no-cause termination is less than the more common 30-60 day range.

clause_text: Tenant agrees to vacate immediately upon landlord's request, without recourse to legal process.
rationale: Attempts to contractually waive tenant's right to due legal eviction process, which cannot be lawfully waived.

clause_text: Landlord may forcibly remove tenant's belongings and re-let the premises if rent is delayed beyond 7 days.
rationale: Self-help eviction and forcible removal of belongings is illegal regardless of rent delay duration.

clause_text: Landlord may disconnect water and electricity supply to compel the tenant to vacate.
rationale: Utility disconnection as a pressure tactic to force eviction is a widely recognized illegal practice.

clause_text: In the event of termination, both parties shall settle outstanding dues and hand over/accept vacant possession within 7 days.
rationale: Clear, balanced handover process with a reasonable timeline.

clause_text: Tenant shall be liable for the remaining lock-in period's rent in full if agreement is terminated early, regardless of reason.
rationale: 'Regardless of reason' framing is inflexible even for legitimate emergencies; common but tenant-unfavorable.

clause_text: Tenant waives all rights to legal notice or hearing in case of eviction for any reason whatsoever.
rationale: Blanket waiver of legal notice/hearing rights is unenforceable; due process cannot be contractually waived.

clause_text: Eviction proceedings, if any, shall be conducted through the Rent Controller as prescribed under the Delhi Rent Control Act, 1958, ensuring due process for the tenant.
rationale: Correctly reflects the due-process requirement for Act-covered tenancy eviction.

clause_text: Security deposit of 2 months' rent to be refunded within 10 days of vacation, subject to deduction for unpaid utility bills and damages beyond normal wear and tear.
rationale: Quick refund, standard deposit amount, and deductions limited to legitimate items.

clause_text: Deposit equivalent to 4 months' rent, refundable within 60 days after deduction for any repair costs as determined by landlord.
rationale: 4 months is above typical 2-3 month range; 60-day refund is long; landlord's sole determination lacks transparency.

clause_text: Security deposit shall be 3 months' rent and shall be refunded within 30 days of the tenant vacating, provided the tenant has given proper notice.
rationale: Standard deposit amount and reasonable refund timeline; condition of proper notice is usual.

clause_text: Deposit of 8 months' rent shall be held as security and refunded within 45 days after deducting all outstanding dues.
rationale: 8 months is a significant outlier; 45 days is longer than typical, though not illegal; caution warranted.

clause_text: Security deposit shall be adjusted against the last three months' rent, and no refund shall be made.
rationale: Adjustment against final rent without any refund or surplus handling leaves tenant with no right to excess deposit, which is unfair.

clause_text: Deposit of 2 months' rent to be refunded within 30 days of vacating, with a detailed statement of deductions provided.
rationale: Standard deposit, reasonable timeline, and requirement for itemized deduction statement.

clause_text: Tenant shall pay a security deposit of 6 months' rent, which shall be non-refundable in case of any breach by tenant.
rationale: 6 months is above market norm; non-refundable for 'any breach' is overly broad and may lead to unfair forfeiture.

clause_text: Security deposit of 3 months' rent shall be refunded within 15 days of vacating, subject to deduction for unpaid rent and utilities only.
rationale: Standard deposit, prompt refund, and deductions explicitly limited to rent and utilities.

clause_text: Deposit equal to 10 months' rent shall be collected and refunded within 90 days of vacating, with interest at 5% per annum.
rationale: 10 months is highly extreme; 90-day refund is very long; even with interest, this deviates drastically from market practice.

clause_text: Security deposit shall be kept in a separate bank account and returned within 21 days of vacating, with an itemized list of deductions.
rationale: Good practice: separate account, prompt refund, and itemized deductions enhance tenant protection.

clause_text: Security deposit shall not exceed the limit prescribed under the Delhi Rent Control Act, 1958, and shall be refunded within 15 days of vacating.
rationale: The DRCA source reviewed does not state a general two-month security-deposit cap. Treating the clause as compliance with a specific DRCA deposit limit could misstate the law.

clause_text: Either party may terminate by giving 60 days' written notice.
rationale: Symmetric, longer notice period is reasonable and gives both parties ample time.

clause_text: Lock-in period of 6 months, early exit allowed with 2 months' notice and forfeiture of 50% of deposit.
rationale: Moderate lock-in, clear early-exit mechanism with a proportionate forfeiture.

clause_text: Tenant shall give 3 months' notice to vacate; landlord may give 30 days' notice.
rationale: Asymmetric notice periods strongly favor the landlord and disadvantage the tenant.

clause_text: Lock-in of 24 months, with no early termination except by mutual consent.
rationale: Very long lock-in period; lack of exit flexibility can be harsh for tenants.

clause_text: Landlord may terminate immediately if tenant causes nuisance, without notice.
rationale: Immediate termination without notice for subjective 'nuisance' bypasses due process and is unenforceable.

clause_text: Tenant must give one month's notice; landlord must give two months' notice.
rationale: Symmetric in favor of tenant; gives tenant extra time to plan, which is fair.

clause_text: Lock-in period of 11 months, tenant may exit early by paying 2 months' rent as penalty.
rationale: Clear early-exit penalty; 2 months' rent is a reasonable charge for breaking the lock-in.

clause_text: No lock-in period; either party may terminate with 15 days' notice.
rationale: Flexible, short notice period; no lock-in gives tenant freedom to vacate easily.

clause_text: Landlord may terminate with 7 days' notice for non-payment of rent.
rationale: 7 days is very short notice for non-payment; although rent default is serious, this may not give tenant time to remedy.

clause_text: Tenant waives all rights to notice before eviction for any reason.
rationale: Blanket waiver of notice rights is unenforceable; eviction requires due process irrespective of contract.

clause_text: Lock-in period of 3 months, with early termination allowed on 30 days' notice without penalty.
rationale: Short lock-in and penalty-free exit after notice is tenant-friendly and reasonable.

clause_text: Tenant to pay for all minor repairs, landlord for major structural repairs.
rationale: Standard split of maintenance responsibilities.

clause_text: Landlord shall be responsible for repairs to the building structure and common areas.
rationale: Clearly assigns structural and common-area repairs to landlord, which is typical.

clause_text: Tenant shall bear cost of all repairs up to Rs. 5000 per year; beyond that landlord pays.
rationale: Caps tenant's repair liability at a reasonable amount, leaving larger expenses to landlord.

clause_text: Landlord shall not be liable for any repairs, including plumbing and electrical.
rationale: Exempting landlord from all repairs, especially essential systems, is extreme and likely unenforceable.

clause_text: Tenant shall maintain the garden and terrace; landlord maintains the building structure.
rationale: Clear division: tenant handles external areas, landlord keeps structural integrity.

clause_text: Any repair request by tenant must be in writing; landlord shall respond within 7 days.
rationale: Requires written request and sets a reasonable response timeline, ensuring accountability.

clause_text: Tenant shall be responsible for all maintenance charges including society fees and property taxes.
rationale: Property taxes are usually borne by landlord; shifting them to tenant is unusual and may be unfair.

clause_text: Landlord shall reimburse tenant for emergency repairs up to Rs. 2000 without prior approval.
rationale: Allows tenant to address emergencies quickly and ensures reimbursement for small amounts.

clause_text: Tenant shall carry out all routine maintenance and major repairs at his own cost, except for defects arising from landlord's negligence.
rationale: Shifting major repairs to tenant is an overreach; only exception is landlord's negligence, which may be difficult to prove.

clause_text: Landlord shall ensure the property is in habitable condition and shall carry out all necessary repairs within a reasonable time.
rationale: Reflects the basic habitability obligation for Act-covered tenancies; reasonable timeline is fair.

clause_text: Tenant shall be responsible for painting and whitewashing at the end of the tenancy.
rationale: Typical clause requiring tenant to restore paint/wash, which is acceptable as it is cosmetic.

clause_text: Rent shall increase by 5% every year, with 2 months' notice.
rationale: Low annual increase and long notice period are fair and predictable.

clause_text: Rent shall increase by 15% annually, with 30 days' notice.
rationale: Higher than typical escalation and short notice make it challenging for tenant to budget.

clause_text: Rent shall be revised every two years based on CPI index.
rationale: Objective, inflation-linked adjustment is transparent and fair.

clause_text: Landlord may increase rent at any time by any amount.
rationale: Unfettered discretion to raise rent without any cap or notice is fundamentally unfair and likely unenforceable.

clause_text: Rent shall increase by 10% every 12 months, with 1 month's notice.
rationale: Common 10% annual escalation with standard notice period.

clause_text: Rent shall remain fixed for 2 years, then may be revised by mutual consent.
rationale: Fixed rent for a considerable period and mutual consent for revision is tenant-friendly.

clause_text: Rent shall increase by 20% every year, with 15 days' notice.
rationale: 20% annual hike is extreme; 15 days notice is insufficient; clearly a high-risk clause.

clause_text: Rent shall increase only upon renewal of the agreement.
rationale: Predictable: rent stays same during the term, changes only at renewal, which is acceptable.

clause_text: Landlord may increase rent by up to 10% every three years, as per DRCA for applicable tenancies.
rationale: Complies with the DRCA rent revision norm for Act-covered tenancies.

clause_text: Rent shall be increased every 6 months at 5%.
rationale: Biannual increases, even if small, create frequent adjustments that may burden the tenant.

clause_text: Rent shall be fixed for the first year, then may be increased by 10% annually with 3 months' notice.
rationale: Initial fixed term followed by a moderate annual increase with ample notice.

clause_text: Either party may terminate with 30 days' notice.
rationale: Standard, symmetric notice period.

clause_text: Tenant shall be evicted for non-payment of rent after 15 days' notice.
rationale: 15 days is short but common; still may not give tenant enough time to pay arrears.

clause_text: Landlord may evict tenant for causing nuisance, with 7 days' notice.
rationale: Short notice and subjective 'nuisance' ground may be abused; caution advised.

clause_text: Tenant shall vacate on expiry of the agreement; no notice required.
rationale: Natural expiry, no notice needed; it's a standard practice.

clause_text: Landlord may lock out tenant for any breach of agreement.
rationale: Self-help lockout is illegal; any breach does not justify forcible exclusion.

clause_text: Eviction shall be carried out only through court order.
rationale: Properly mandates judicial process for eviction in Act-covered tenancies.

clause_text: Tenant shall be liable for all legal costs in case of eviction proceedings.
rationale: While not illegal, shifting all legal costs to tenant could be onerous; common but worth flagging.

clause_text: Landlord may terminate the agreement without cause upon 30 days' notice.
rationale: Symmetric no-cause termination with reasonable notice is acceptable.

clause_text: Tenant shall not be entitled to any compensation or relocation assistance upon eviction.
rationale: No compensation is typical; landlords are not generally required to provide relocation assistance.

clause_text: Agreement terminates automatically upon tenant's death, and heirs must vacate within 15 days.
rationale: Automatic termination upon death may be harsh for heirs; 15 days is short to arrange vacating.

clause_text: Either party may terminate the tenancy by giving one month's notice; no reason required.
rationale: Standard, symmetric no-fault termination.

clause_text: Tenant shall pay a refundable security deposit equal to one month's rent, with deductions limited to documented unpaid dues or tenant-caused damage.
rationale: Low deposit with defined, documented deductions is commercially clear and tenant-protective.

clause_text: Tenant shall pay a refundable security deposit equal to two months' rent, refundable after final meter readings and settlement of documented dues.
rationale: Two months is within common market practice and the settlement process is defined.

clause_text: Tenant shall pay a refundable security deposit equal to three months' rent, with any deduction supported by an itemized statement.
rationale: Three months is a common market benchmark and itemization improves transparency.

clause_text: Tenant shall pay a refundable security deposit equal to four months' rent, refundable within 30 days after vacant possession.
rationale: Four months is above the common 2–3 month benchmark, though it is not by itself a DRCA violation for rent above ₹3,500.

clause_text: Tenant shall pay a refundable security deposit equal to six months' rent, with refund subject to an itemized account of deductions.
rationale: Six months is a significant market outlier and should be negotiated, but the amount is not automatically illegal under the DRCA for rent above ₹3,500.

clause_text: Tenant shall pay a refundable security deposit equal to ten months' rent, refundable within 30 days after handover.
rationale: Ten months is an extreme market outlier and creates substantial tenant exposure even though there is no general DRCA cap for rent above ₹3,500.

clause_text: The security deposit shall be treated as non-refundable once the tenant gives notice to vacate.
rationale: A blanket non-refund rule defeats the ordinary purpose of a refundable security deposit and is heavily tenant-disadvantageous.

clause_text: Landlord may deduct any amount from the security deposit for any reason considered appropriate by the landlord.
rationale: Unlimited unilateral deductions without objective criteria or evidence create an abusive and unpredictable deduction mechanism.

clause_text: The security deposit shall be refunded only after the landlord is fully satisfied with the property's condition, with no maximum refund period.
rationale: A subjective condition combined with no deadline creates a risk of indefinite withholding.

clause_text: Tenant authorizes the landlord to retain the entire deposit for any breach, regardless of the actual financial loss caused.
rationale: Automatic forfeiture regardless of actual loss is disproportionate and exposes the tenant to excessive penalties.

clause_text: For a tenancy at monthly rent of ₹3,500, the parties record a refundable deposit of two months' rent and an itemized deduction process.
rationale: The clause does not invent a DRCA deposit cap and instead clearly defines the deposit and deductions; the DRCA regime should be assessed separately from the deposit amount.

clause_text: For a tenancy at monthly rent of ₹3,500, the agreement states that the DRCA itself limits every security deposit to two months' rent.
rationale: The two-month residential cap belongs to the Model Tenancy Act reference framework, not a general security-deposit cap expressly found in the DRCA; the clause risks conflating regimes.

clause_text: For a tenancy at monthly rent of ₹3,500, the deposit shall be refundable after deduction of proven rent arrears and documented tenant-caused damage.
rationale: The deduction language is specific and avoids attributing a Model Tenancy Act deposit cap to the DRCA.

clause_text: For a tenancy at monthly rent of ₹3,500, the landlord may retain the deposit indefinitely until a future inspection date chosen solely by the landlord.
rationale: An indefinite, unilateral withholding mechanism is materially unfair and should be flagged regardless of the applicable rent-control regime.

clause_text: For a tenancy at monthly rent of ₹3,500, the landlord shall provide an itemized statement for every deduction from the deposit.
rationale: Itemization improves accountability and is consistent with a transparent deposit-settlement process.

clause_text: Security deposit shall be increased automatically whenever rent increases, without a separate written record.
rationale: Automatic recalculation can create uncertainty if the revised deposit is not clearly documented.

clause_text: The deposit shall be converted into advance rent for the final three months unless the landlord elects otherwise.
rationale: Mixing refundable security with advance rent creates ambiguity about refund rights and settlement accounting.

clause_text: Landlord may use the security deposit to cover ordinary repainting and replacement required solely by normal wear and tear.
rationale: Charging ordinary wear and tear against the deposit is tenant-unfavorable and conflicts with the usual distinction between damage and normal use.

clause_text: No portion of the security deposit may be adjusted against rent during the tenancy unless both parties agree in writing.
rationale: A clear written-consent rule prevents unilateral conversion of the deposit into rent.

clause_text: The deposit shall be held by the landlord without any requirement to maintain records of deductions or supporting invoices.
rationale: Removing basic deduction records makes disputes difficult to verify and materially weakens tenant protection.

clause_text: If utility bills are pending at handover, the landlord may retain only the reasonably estimated amount and must reconcile it after the final bill.
rationale: Temporary retention tied to an estimated liability with later reconciliation is proportionate and transparent.

clause_text: If the tenant leaves before the lock-in expires, the entire security deposit shall automatically become the landlord's property.
rationale: Automatic full forfeiture combines deposit treatment with a penalty and can be disproportionate to actual loss.

clause_text: The landlord shall return the undisputed portion of the security deposit first and settle disputed deductions separately.
rationale: Returning the undisputed amount reduces unnecessary withholding and separates genuine disputes from uncontested sums.

clause_text: The tenant shall receive a written deposit receipt showing the amount paid, date received, and whether it is refundable.
rationale: Clear documentation reduces later disputes about whether a payment was security, advance rent, or another charge.

clause_text: The deposit shall be refunded within 15 days after handover, subject to documented deductions for identified liabilities.
rationale: A defined short refund period and documented deductions provide a predictable settlement process.

clause_text: Either party may terminate the agreement with 30 days' written notice after the initial three-month lock-in.
rationale: A short, symmetric notice mechanism with a limited lock-in is predictable.

clause_text: Tenant must give 60 days' notice while landlord must give 30 days' notice for no-cause termination.
rationale: The asymmetric notice burden favors the landlord and reduces tenant flexibility.

clause_text: The tenant may exit during a six-month lock-in by giving 30 days' notice and paying one month's rent as an agreed early-exit charge.
rationale: The lock-in and exit cost are clearly defined and proportionate.

clause_text: The tenant may not terminate during an eleven-month lock-in under any circumstances.
rationale: An absolute lock-in removes flexibility for emergencies and relocation and should be negotiated carefully.

clause_text: The landlord may terminate immediately whenever the landlord considers the tenant's conduct inconvenient.
rationale: Subjective immediate termination gives the landlord unilateral power without an objective breach standard.

clause_text: Tenant waives every notice right and agrees to vacate whenever the landlord sends a demand.
rationale: A blanket contractual waiver of legal protections and due process is highly problematic.

clause_text: The lock-in period shall automatically renew for another twelve months unless the tenant gives notice six months before expiry.
rationale: Long automatic renewal and an unusually early notice deadline can trap a tenant unintentionally.

clause_text: Either party may terminate after the lock-in with 45 days' written notice.
rationale: A symmetric, clearly stated post-lock-in notice period is commercially reasonable.

clause_text: Early termination by the tenant will incur a fixed charge equal to one month's rent, regardless of remaining lock-in duration.
rationale: A fixed and disclosed early-exit charge is more predictable than an unlimited claim for future rent.

clause_text: Early termination by the tenant requires payment of every remaining month's rent through the end of the lease term.
rationale: A full remaining-term claim can be harsh and should be evaluated against the actual contractual structure and mitigation of loss.

clause_text: A tenancy at monthly rent of ₹3,500 may be terminated only through the process applicable to the DRCA-covered tenancy.
rationale: The clause correctly recognizes that the statutory regime must be checked before relying on ordinary contractual termination language.

clause_text: A tenancy at monthly rent of ₹3,500 may be ended immediately by the landlord merely because the tenant has requested repairs.
rationale: Using a repair request as a trigger for immediate termination is retaliatory and conflicts with basic contractual fairness.

clause_text: A tenancy at monthly rent of ₹3,500 shall provide the tenant one month to cure a specified non-payment default after written demand.
rationale: A defined cure mechanism is more consistent with a due-process-oriented rent-control framework than immediate self-help.

clause_text: A tenancy at monthly rent of ₹3,500 shall allow the landlord to change the locks immediately after any missed payment.
rationale: Self-help lockout is not an appropriate substitute for the statutory eviction process.

clause_text: The lock-in shall apply equally to landlord and tenant, and either party leaving early will follow the same agreed notice mechanism.
rationale: Mutuality reduces one-sided termination risk.

clause_text: The landlord may terminate on seven days' notice but the tenant must give ninety days' notice.
rationale: The strongly asymmetric notice periods create a material imbalance.

clause_text: Notice is valid only if sent by email and acknowledged by the recipient within 24 hours.
rationale: Requiring affirmative acknowledgment can make otherwise valid notice ineffective through non-response.

clause_text: Notice may be delivered by email, registered post, or another agreed written method, with the effective date recorded.
rationale: Multiple documented delivery methods improve certainty and reduce disputes over notice.

clause_text: A lock-in penalty shall apply even where the landlord materially breaches an agreed obligation.
rationale: Applying the same penalty despite a landlord breach can create an unfair one-sided risk allocation.

clause_text: The tenant may terminate without penalty if the premises become materially uninhabitable and the landlord fails to remedy the condition within a reasonable cure period.
rationale: A defined remedy for serious habitability failure provides a balanced contractual exit mechanism.

clause_text: The notice period begins only after the landlord confirms receipt in writing.
rationale: Making notice effective only on discretionary confirmation can create avoidable uncertainty.

clause_text: A tenant who transfers employment outside Delhi may terminate with 30 days' notice and no additional lock-in penalty.
rationale: A defined relocation exception creates practical flexibility without making the agreement open-ended.

clause_text: The lock-in period ends automatically if both parties sign a written termination agreement.
rationale: Express mutual waiver of the lock-in is clear and reduces disputes.

clause_text: Notice served before the lock-in expires shall be treated as invalid even if the actual termination date falls after the lock-in.
rationale: Invalidating early notice can create unnecessary timing traps and prolong tenancy disputes.

clause_text: The agreement has no lock-in, and either party may terminate with 30 days' written notice.
rationale: A simple no-lock-in structure with equal notice is clear and flexible.

clause_text: Landlord shall handle structural repairs and tenant shall handle routine replacement of consumable items.
rationale: The allocation distinguishes structural responsibility from ordinary consumables.

clause_text: Tenant shall pay for minor repairs up to ₹2,000 per incident, while landlord bears larger structural repairs.
rationale: A monetary threshold creates a clear division of routine and major repair costs.

clause_text: Tenant shall pay for every repair, including defects caused by the building's age.
rationale: The clause shifts age-related building defects to the tenant and is materially tenant-unfavorable.

clause_text: Landlord shall repair major plumbing leaks within a reasonable time after written notice.
rationale: Major plumbing defects are appropriately assigned to the landlord with a notice mechanism.

clause_text: Tenant shall be responsible for all electrical wiring failures regardless of whether they pre-date the tenancy.
rationale: Making the tenant liable for pre-existing structural or wiring defects creates an unreasonable risk transfer.

clause_text: Landlord may deduct any repair amount without showing invoices if the landlord believes the repair was necessary.
rationale: Unverified unilateral deductions create a serious transparency problem.

clause_text: Tenant shall maintain appliances supplied with the premises, excluding replacement caused by ordinary age-related failure.
rationale: The clause separates tenant maintenance from normal end-of-life replacement.

clause_text: The tenant shall repaint the premises every six months at the tenant's cost regardless of condition.
rationale: Mandatory repainting at fixed intervals regardless of need is unusual and may impose unnecessary cost.

clause_text: Landlord shall be responsible for water seepage originating from building structure.
rationale: Structural seepage is appropriately assigned to the property owner.

clause_text: Tenant shall report urgent repair issues promptly and provide reasonable access for the repair.
rationale: Prompt reporting and access duties create a balanced repair workflow.

clause_text: For premises at monthly rent of ₹3,500, landlord shall maintain the property in a condition fit for occupation, subject to the applicable statutory framework.
rationale: The clause preserves the habitability concept without attributing an unsupported detailed repair schedule to the DRCA.

clause_text: For premises at monthly rent of ₹3,500, tenant shall bear structural repairs even when the defect existed before possession.
rationale: Pre-existing structural defects should not be shifted wholesale to the tenant merely by contract wording.

clause_text: Landlord shall reimburse emergency repairs reasonably necessary to prevent immediate property damage when prior approval is impracticable.
rationale: The exception allows emergency action while keeping reimbursement tied to necessity.

clause_text: Tenant shall obtain three quotations before any repair, including emergency plumbing work.
rationale: A rigid quotation requirement can delay necessary emergency repairs.

clause_text: Landlord shall respond to a written non-emergency repair request within seven days.
rationale: A response deadline improves accountability without guaranteeing an unrealistic completion time.

clause_text: Tenant shall bear society maintenance charges but landlord shall bear property tax unless expressly agreed otherwise.
rationale: The split reflects a common contractual allocation and clearly identifies the owner-side tax obligation.

clause_text: Tenant shall pay property tax directly to the municipality without receiving any corresponding rent adjustment.
rationale: Shifting owner-side tax costs without explaining the economic allocation can materially increase tenant cost.

clause_text: Landlord shall replace a failed water heater supplied with the premises when failure is not caused by tenant misuse.
rationale: The clause distinguishes equipment failure from tenant-caused damage.

clause_text: Tenant shall pay for every appliance replacement, even where the appliance fails due to normal deterioration.
rationale: The clause makes the tenant responsible for ordinary depreciation and replacement.

clause_text: The tenant must obtain landlord approval before engaging a repair contractor except in emergencies.
rationale: Approval control is reasonable when paired with an emergency exception.

clause_text: Landlord shall have no responsibility for repairs to essential water or electrical systems.
rationale: A blanket exclusion of essential-system repairs creates serious habitability and safety concerns.

clause_text: Repair deductions from the deposit shall be based on actual reasonable cost rather than a predetermined penalty.
rationale: Tying deductions to actual reasonable cost limits arbitrary penalties.

clause_text: Tenant shall be liable for damage caused by guests, but not for ordinary wear and tear.
rationale: The clause identifies responsibility for guest-caused damage while preserving the normal-wear distinction.

clause_text: The landlord may enter the premises to inspect repairs without giving prior notice.
rationale: Unrestricted entry is a separate privacy and possession concern and should be controlled by reasonable notice.

clause_text: Tenant shall maintain cleanliness and minor consumables but shall not be responsible for latent structural defects.
rationale: The distinction between routine upkeep and latent defects is clear and balanced.

clause_text: Rent shall increase by 5% annually after the first twelve months, with 60 days' written notice.
rationale: Moderate annual escalation with substantial notice is predictable and common.

clause_text: Rent shall increase by 10% annually with one month's written notice.
rationale: A defined annual increase and notice period are transparent and common in market agreements.

clause_text: Rent shall increase by 15% annually with 15 days' notice.
rationale: The increase is relatively high and the notice period is short.

clause_text: Rent may be increased by any amount whenever the landlord believes market rates have changed.
rationale: Unbounded unilateral escalation creates severe contractual uncertainty.

clause_text: Rent shall remain fixed during the eleven-month term and may be renegotiated only on renewal.
rationale: The clause provides clear price certainty during the fixed term.

clause_text: Rent shall increase by 25% every six months.
rationale: Frequent and very large increases are extreme market deviations and materially increase tenant exposure.

clause_text: Rent revision shall be based on a specified CPI-linked formula every two years.
rationale: An objective index-based formula reduces discretionary escalation risk.

clause_text: Rent shall increase by 7% annually, but the landlord may add a further discretionary increase at any time.
rationale: The fixed component is clear but the additional discretionary increase creates uncertainty.

clause_text: Any rent increase must be agreed in writing by both parties before it becomes effective.
rationale: Written mutual agreement provides a clear record and limits surprise increases.

clause_text: The tenant shall accept any rent increase notified seven days before the next rental period.
rationale: Seven days provides little planning time and leaves the increase largely one-sided.

clause_text: For rent of ₹3,500, the agreement shall apply the statutory revision framework rather than a market-style automatic escalation.
rationale: This correctly directs the analysis toward the DRCA framework for a potentially covered tenancy.

clause_text: For rent of ₹3,500, rent shall increase by 10% every three years with the required written notice process.
rationale: This tracks the DRCA Section 6A/8 framework reflected in the primary text and judicial discussion.

clause_text: For rent of ₹3,500, rent shall increase by 10% every year automatically.
rationale: An annual automatic increase conflicts with the DRCA's ten-per-cent-every-three-years revision rule for covered premises.

clause_text: For rent of ₹3,500, rent shall increase by 30% every year without written notice.
rationale: The clause departs sharply from the DRCA revision framework in both magnitude and notice.

clause_text: For rent of ₹3,500, the landlord may increase rent whenever the local market rises, without reference to the statutory regime.
rationale: The clause ignores the applicable rent-control framework and grants unbounded escalation discretion.

clause_text: For rent above ₹3,500, the agreement states that the DRCA automatically caps annual rent increases at 10%.
rationale: This incorrectly extends the DRCA rent-revision rule to premises excluded from the Act by Section 3(c).

clause_text: For rent above ₹3,500, rent shall increase by 8% annually as expressly agreed in the lease.
rationale: A defined contractual escalation above the DRCA threshold is primarily a contract term, not a DRCA statutory cap issue.

clause_text: For rent above ₹3,500, rent shall increase by 12% every two years with 90 days' notice.
rationale: The clause is explicit, infrequent, and supported by substantial notice; it is a negotiable contract term.

clause_text: For rent above ₹3,500, the landlord may revise rent only at renewal and must give the proposed amount before renewal discussions.
rationale: The clause preserves price certainty during the term and gives advance notice for renewal.

clause_text: For rent above ₹3,500, rent shall increase by 20% every six months without a market benchmark.
rationale: The frequency and magnitude are strong market outliers and create substantial tenant exposure.

clause_text: Rent escalation shall be suspended while the landlord is in material breach of a promised essential service.
rationale: The remedy may be useful but should be clearly defined to avoid disputes about what constitutes a material breach.

clause_text: The escalation percentage shall apply to base rent only and not to separately itemized utility reimbursements.
rationale: Separating rent from pass-through charges prevents accidental compounding of unrelated costs.

clause_text: The landlord may compound an annual rent increase onto all previous increases without stating the calculation method.
rationale: Ambiguous compounding language can create unexpected rent calculations.

clause_text: Rent shall increase by 5% after the first year and then remain fixed for the remaining term.
rationale: A single defined adjustment is easy to understand and budget for.

clause_text: Any rent revision must identify the effective date, revised amount, and calculation basis in the written notice.
rationale: The clause improves transparency and reduces disputes over how the revised rent was calculated.

clause_text: Landlord may terminate the tenancy for a material breach after giving written notice describing the breach and a reasonable opportunity to cure.
rationale: A defined breach-and-cure mechanism is more balanced than immediate self-help termination.

clause_text: Landlord may remove the tenant's belongings immediately after seven days of rent delay.
rationale: Forcible removal of belongings is self-help eviction and should not be used as a contractual shortcut.

clause_text: Landlord may disconnect electricity to compel the tenant to vacate after a payment dispute.
rationale: Utility disconnection as pressure for eviction is an abusive self-help measure.

clause_text: Tenant agrees to vacate immediately whenever the landlord claims a breach, without court or other lawful process.
rationale: A contractual waiver of lawful eviction process is highly problematic.

clause_text: Either party may terminate for convenience with 30 days' written notice.
rationale: Symmetric no-cause termination is clear when the tenancy is outside statutory rent control.

clause_text: Landlord may terminate without cause on seven days' notice while tenant must give 60 days.
rationale: The imbalance materially favors the landlord.

clause_text: Tenant remains liable for rent after termination only until the agreed termination date, subject to other accrued liabilities.
rationale: The clause avoids an automatic claim for unearned future rent while preserving accrued obligations.

clause_text: Tenant shall pay all remaining rent through the fixed term even if the landlord re-lets the property immediately.
rationale: The clause may create double-recovery concerns and should be evaluated against actual loss and mitigation.

clause_text: The agreement ends automatically upon any complaint by a neighbor, without investigation.
rationale: Automatic termination based on an unverified complaint is arbitrary and lacks a fair breach process.

clause_text: Eviction shall be carried out through the legally applicable forum and process rather than by changing locks.
rationale: The clause expressly rejects self-help eviction and preserves lawful process.

clause_text: For rent of ₹3,500, eviction shall be assessed against the grounds and process applicable under Section 14 of the DRCA.
rationale: The clause correctly directs analysis to the DRCA's statutory eviction framework for covered premises.

clause_text: For rent of ₹3,500, landlord may evict immediately for any disagreement about repairs.
rationale: A generic disagreement is not a substitute for the statutory grounds and process governing covered tenancies.

clause_text: For rent of ₹3,500, landlord may change the locks after a missed payment without approaching the Rent Controller.
rationale: The clause substitutes self-help for the statutory eviction process.

clause_text: For rent of ₹3,500, the tenant shall have no opportunity to contest an eviction claim.
rationale: Removing the tenant's ability to contest a statutory proceeding is inconsistent with due process.

clause_text: For rent of ₹3,500, arrears shall be documented and handled through the payment and eviction mechanisms applicable under the DRCA.
rationale: The clause avoids inventing a private eviction shortcut and recognizes the statutory framework.

clause_text: Landlord may take possession of the property immediately after sending a termination email.
rationale: A termination notice does not by itself justify forcible physical recovery of possession.

clause_text: The tenant shall return keys on the agreed termination date and landlord shall acknowledge receipt in writing.
rationale: Documented handover reduces disputes about possession and termination.

clause_text: If either party materially breaches the agreement, the non-breaching party may seek contractual remedies available under applicable law.
rationale: The clause preserves lawful remedies without authorizing self-help.

clause_text: Landlord may seize tenant property left behind without providing a collection or notice period.
rationale: Unregulated seizure of belongings creates significant legal and practical risk.

clause_text: Termination is effective only after outstanding possession, rent, and documented utility obligations are reconciled.
rationale: Linking legal termination to complete reconciliation may create disputes if one side delays settlement.

clause_text: A termination notice must identify the effective date and the contractual basis for termination.
rationale: Specific notice content improves certainty and reduces factual disputes.

clause_text: The landlord may terminate for repeated nuisance after two written warnings describing the conduct.
rationale: Objective warnings and a defined escalation process are more balanced than immediate termination.

clause_text: The landlord may terminate whenever the tenant receives a police complaint, regardless of whether wrongdoing is established.
rationale: A mere complaint is not proof of breach and should not automatically trigger forfeiture of tenancy.

clause_text: The tenant may terminate if the landlord repeatedly prevents access to essential services promised under the agreement.
rationale: A defined tenant remedy for material landlord interference creates contractual balance.

clause_text: On expiry, the parties shall record the date of vacant possession, meter readings, key return, and outstanding amounts.
rationale: A documented exit record is useful for resolving deposit and possession disputes.

clause_text: Rent is payable by the fifth day of each calendar month by bank transfer to the account identified in the agreement.
rationale: The due date and payment channel are specific and verifiable.

clause_text: Rent shall be paid in cash without a receipt unless the landlord chooses to issue one.
rationale: Lack of a mandatory receipt creates avoidable proof and accounting disputes.

clause_text: Electronic payment acknowledgment shall serve as evidence of rent payment.
rationale: Electronic records provide a reliable payment trail.

clause_text: Late rent shall attract a fixed late fee of ₹500 after a five-day grace period.
rationale: A disclosed, modest late fee with a grace period is clearer than an uncapped penalty.

clause_text: Late rent shall attract a penalty of 10% of monthly rent for every day of delay.
rationale: A daily 10% penalty is disproportionate and can rapidly create an excessive liability.

clause_text: Landlord may refuse to issue a rent receipt if payment is made after the due date.
rationale: Payment records should not be withheld merely because payment was late.

clause_text: If the landlord refuses rent, the tenant shall preserve evidence of the tender and use any legally available deposit or dispute mechanism.
rationale: This reflects the DRCA's statutory mechanisms for rent tender and deposit without inventing a private remedy.

clause_text: For rent of ₹3,500, the tenant shall pay rent by the fifteenth day of the following month when no different contractual date applies.
rationale: This tracks the DRCA payment rule where no contractual payment time is specified.

clause_text: For rent of ₹3,500, landlord may declare eviction automatically one day after rent is late.
rationale: Automatic eviction bypasses the statutory framework for arrears and eviction.

clause_text: For rent of ₹3,500, landlord shall provide a written receipt for rent received.
rationale: Receipt entitlement is expressly addressed by the DRCA.

clause_text: Tenant shall pay rent to a property manager, and payment to that manager shall be treated as payment to the landlord.
rationale: The clause clarifies the authorized payment recipient and reduces payment disputes.

clause_text: Rent may be withheld whenever the tenant has a non-rent complaint against the landlord.
rationale: Unilateral rent withholding can create default disputes; separate remedies should be defined instead.

clause_text: Rent shall be paid only after the landlord completes all requested repairs.
rationale: Making rent entirely contingent on repair completion can create a separate payment default dispute.

clause_text: A failed bank transfer shall be treated as unpaid unless the tenant provides proof that the amount was successfully credited.
rationale: The clause establishes a clear payment-verification rule.

clause_text: Landlord shall notify the tenant of a changed bank account at least seven days before the next due date.
rationale: Advance notice reduces fraud and accidental non-payment risk.

clause_text: Tenant shall not be charged a convenience fee for paying rent by the agreed electronic method.
rationale: The clause avoids an unexplained payment surcharge.

clause_text: Landlord may demand six months' rent in advance at any time during the tenancy without written agreement.
rationale: A unilateral demand for a large advance changes the agreed payment structure and should be negotiated.

clause_text: The parties shall distinguish rent, security deposit, utility reimbursement, and maintenance charges in every payment record.
rationale: Separating payment categories improves accounting and dispute resolution.

clause_text: A payment received shall first be applied to the oldest undisputed rent, then to agreed charges.
rationale: A stated allocation order reduces disputes about how partial payments are credited.

clause_text: Tenant shall provide post-dated cheques for the full lease term, with no alternative payment method.
rationale: A rigid long-term cheque requirement can create practical and financial risk for the tenant.

clause_text: Landlord may encash all post-dated cheques immediately after any minor breach.
rationale: Using future rent instruments as an automatic penalty for unrelated minor breaches is excessive.

clause_text: Rent shall be considered paid when the transfer is initiated rather than when funds are credited.
rationale: The rule can create ambiguity where a transfer fails or is delayed by the banking system.

clause_text: If rent is disputed, the undisputed portion shall remain payable while the disputed amount is handled separately.
rationale: Separating undisputed rent from disputed amounts is a balanced contractual approach.

clause_text: The landlord shall issue an annual statement summarizing rent received and outstanding amounts.
rationale: Periodic statements improve recordkeeping and reduce later reconciliation disputes.

clause_text: Rent shall be paid to the landlord's designated account, and any account change must be confirmed in writing.
rationale: Written confirmation of payment-account changes reduces fraud and mistaken payments.

clause_text: Landlord may enter the premises for inspection after giving at least 24 hours' written notice, except in emergencies.
rationale: Advance notice with an emergency exception balances inspection rights and tenant privacy.

clause_text: Landlord may enter the premises at any time without notice.
rationale: Unrestricted entry materially interferes with the tenant's peaceful possession and privacy.

clause_text: Landlord may conduct one routine inspection every six months with reasonable prior notice.
rationale: Periodic inspections with notice are commercially reasonable.

clause_text: Landlord may bring prospective purchasers into the premises every day during the final month without coordinating with the tenant.
rationale: Frequent uncoordinated access can materially interfere with possession.

clause_text: Tenant must permit emergency access where delay could cause serious injury or property damage.
rationale: An emergency-access exception is reasonable and narrowly defined.

clause_text: Landlord may retain a duplicate key and use it whenever the tenant is away.
rationale: Unrestricted use of retained keys undermines tenant control over possession.

clause_text: Inspection requests must identify the purpose and proposed time of entry.
rationale: Clear notice content improves predictability.

clause_text: Landlord may enter for photography without consent to advertise the property for sale.
rationale: Marketing access and photography can raise privacy concerns and should be coordinated.

clause_text: Tenant shall not unreasonably refuse access for necessary repairs after reasonable notice.
rationale: The clause balances tenant possession with legitimate repair access.

clause_text: Landlord may enter with police assistance whenever the tenant does not answer the door.
rationale: Non-response is not itself a lawful basis for coercive entry.

clause_text: For rent of ₹3,500, landlord entry shall remain subject to the tenant's possession rights and the applicable statutory framework.
rationale: The clause avoids inventing a special DRCA entry rule while preserving the need for lawful access.

clause_text: For rent of ₹3,500, landlord may enter every morning without notice to check the property.
rationale: Routine unannounced entry materially interferes with possession and is not justified merely by the rent bracket.

clause_text: Landlord shall give reasonable notice before non-emergency access, with shorter notice only where urgent action is genuinely required.
rationale: The distinction between routine and urgent access is practical and balanced.

clause_text: Tenant may request that routine inspections occur during agreed daytime hours.
rationale: Scheduling inspections reduces disruption without eliminating landlord access.

clause_text: Landlord may install cameras inside the leased bedroom and living area for security monitoring.
rationale: Indoor surveillance of a tenant's private living space creates a severe privacy concern.

clause_text: Landlord may inspect common areas without entering the tenant's private rooms.
rationale: The clause distinguishes legitimate property oversight from unnecessary intrusion.

clause_text: A repair contractor may enter only after the landlord or tenant has confirmed the appointment.
rationale: Confirmation improves security and accountability.

clause_text: If an emergency requires entry while the tenant is absent, landlord shall document the reason and notify the tenant afterward.
rationale: Post-entry documentation creates accountability for emergency access.

clause_text: Landlord may use the tenant's keys to show the property to prospective tenants without notice.
rationale: Unannounced showings interfere with possession and create a security concern.

clause_text: Tenant shall keep access pathways clear so that authorized maintenance can be performed.
rationale: The clause imposes a practical cooperation duty tied to legitimate maintenance.

clause_text: Landlord shall not enter solely to verify whether the tenant has guests unless there is a specific contractual or legal basis.
rationale: The clause limits intrusive monitoring and protects ordinary residential use.

clause_text: The parties shall maintain a written record of repeated access disputes before escalating the matter.
rationale: Documentation helps resolve recurring access disagreements.

clause_text: Landlord may inspect utility meters after giving reasonable notice.
rationale: Meter inspection is a legitimate purpose when conducted with reasonable notice.

clause_text: Tenant shall provide access for mandatory building or safety inspections when legally required.
rationale: The clause recognizes legitimate third-party or statutory inspection requirements.

clause_text: Landlord may enter whenever a rent payment is late, even if no inspection or repair is required.
rationale: Payment default does not justify unrestricted physical access to the premises.

clause_text: Tenant shall pay electricity charges based on the actual meter reading shown on the utility bill.
rationale: Charging actual metered consumption is transparent.

clause_text: Tenant shall pay a fixed electricity surcharge regardless of actual consumption.
rationale: A fixed surcharge can overcharge the tenant unless the calculation and purpose are clear.

clause_text: Landlord shall not disconnect essential utilities as a means of enforcing rent payment.
rationale: The clause expressly prevents coercive self-help.

clause_text: Tenant shall pay society maintenance charges directly to the society where the society permits direct payment.
rationale: Direct payment can improve transparency when the society permits it.

clause_text: Landlord may add any utility charge at any time without providing the underlying bill.
rationale: Unverified pass-through charges create an opaque payment obligation.

clause_text: Water charges shall be allocated according to the society's documented billing method.
rationale: A documented allocation method reduces arbitrary charging.

clause_text: Property tax shall be treated as a landlord-side ownership expense unless the parties expressly allocate it otherwise in writing.
rationale: The clause clearly separates ownership costs from tenant consumption.

clause_text: Tenant shall reimburse property tax without any cap or supporting statement.
rationale: Unbounded reimbursement creates uncertainty and may shift substantial ownership costs.

clause_text: If a utility bill covers periods before and after handover, the parties shall prorate the amount by the relevant occupancy dates.
rationale: Proration is a fair method for mixed-period bills.

clause_text: Landlord may retain the entire security deposit for any unpaid utility bill, regardless of the amount owed.
rationale: The remedy is disproportionate to the stated liability.

clause_text: Tenant shall not be charged for utility arrears attributable to periods before possession.
rationale: The clause correctly allocates charges by occupancy period.

clause_text: Tenant shall provide meter readings at move-in and move-out and retain photographs where practical.
rationale: Evidence at handover reduces later billing disputes.

clause_text: Landlord may charge a utility administration fee of ₹1,500 per month without disclosing the underlying cost.
rationale: An unexplained recurring administration fee may conceal additional rent or markup.

clause_text: Electricity shall be billed at the utility provider's applicable tariff without additional markup.
rationale: Passing through the actual tariff is transparent.

clause_text: Landlord may disconnect water for a payment dispute without first obtaining lawful authority.
rationale: Essential-service disconnection as leverage is an abusive enforcement mechanism.

clause_text: Tenant shall pay internet and optional services only when separately subscribed to by the tenant.
rationale: The clause prevents automatic charging for optional services.

clause_text: Common-area electricity charges shall be allocated according to the society's published billing statement.
rationale: Using the society's documented statement creates an objective basis.

clause_text: Tenant shall bear all municipal penalties relating to the property even if caused by the owner's prior non-compliance.
rationale: The clause transfers owner-caused historical liabilities to the tenant.

clause_text: Tenant shall pay charges arising from the tenant's own excessive or negligent utility use.
rationale: The liability is tied to tenant-caused consumption rather than general ownership costs.

clause_text: Any disputed utility charge shall be supported by the underlying bill before deduction from the deposit.
rationale: Document support improves the legitimacy of deductions.

clause_text: For rent of ₹3,500, rent-control applicability does not by itself determine how privately contracted utility charges are allocated.
rationale: The clause prevents the model from treating every utility allocation issue as a DRCA rule.

clause_text: For rent of ₹3,500, landlord may disconnect electricity immediately if rent is late.
rationale: The rent bracket does not justify self-help utility disconnection.

clause_text: Tenant shall pay gas charges directly to the provider where an individual connection exists.
rationale: Direct provider payment creates a clear audit trail.

clause_text: Landlord shall provide copies of recurring utility bills on reasonable request.
rationale: Bill access supports transparent pass-through charging.

clause_text: No utility reimbursement shall be charged twice under both a fixed monthly fee and a separate meter calculation.
rationale: The clause prevents double recovery for the same consumption.

clause_text: Tenant shall use the premises solely for residential purposes and shall not conduct a commercial activity without written consent.
rationale: The permitted-use boundary is clear.

clause_text: Tenant may sublet the premises to any third party without informing the landlord.
rationale: Unrestricted subletting changes possession and counterparty risk.

clause_text: Tenant shall not assign the agreement without the landlord's prior written consent.
rationale: A consent requirement is common and clearly stated.

clause_text: Tenant may host ordinary guests without treating them as sub-tenants.
rationale: The clause distinguishes normal guest use from a transfer of possession.

clause_text: Any guest staying more than seven days automatically becomes a prohibited sub-tenant.
rationale: A rigid duration test can misclassify ordinary family or guest arrangements.

clause_text: Tenant shall not use the premises for an unlawful purpose.
rationale: The clause reinforces a basic lawful-use requirement.

clause_text: Tenant may operate a home office that does not create customer traffic, nuisance, or material property impact.
rationale: A narrowly defined home-office allowance accommodates ordinary modern use.

clause_text: Tenant shall not keep pets under any circumstances, including medically necessary assistance animals.
rationale: A blanket prohibition can create fairness and accommodation concerns and should be drafted carefully.

clause_text: Tenant may not change the internal layout or make structural alterations without written approval.
rationale: Structural changes warrant owner approval.

clause_text: Tenant may paint interior walls only with prior written consent.
rationale: The clause protects the property's condition while allowing negotiated changes.

clause_text: For rent of ₹3,500, subletting restrictions shall be read consistently with the statutory framework applicable to covered premises.
rationale: The clause directs analysis to the DRCA rather than treating a private prohibition as the entire legal answer.

clause_text: For rent of ₹3,500, tenant may be evicted immediately merely because a family member moves into the premises.
rationale: Family occupancy alone should not be treated as an automatic private eviction trigger without considering the applicable legal framework.

clause_text: Tenant shall not transfer possession to another person without written consent and documentation of the new occupant.
rationale: The clause provides a transparent process for changes in occupancy.

clause_text: Tenant shall notify landlord of any adult occupant who will reside at the premises for more than 30 days.
rationale: A long-term occupancy notification rule is clearer than treating every guest as a sub-tenant.

clause_text: Landlord may enter and inspect whenever the tenant has guests.
rationale: Guest presence does not justify unrestricted entry.

clause_text: Tenant may not use the premises for short-term accommodation or paid lodging without written consent.
rationale: The clause addresses a specific commercial-use risk without banning ordinary guests.

clause_text: Tenant shall comply with applicable society rules communicated in writing, provided they do not contradict the agreement or law.
rationale: The qualification prevents hidden or conflicting rules from automatically overriding the agreement.

clause_text: Landlord may terminate immediately if the tenant has a guest who stays overnight.
rationale: Automatic termination for an ordinary overnight guest is disproportionate.

clause_text: Tenant shall not store hazardous materials prohibited by law or building rules.
rationale: The restriction is tied to objective safety and legal requirements.

clause_text: Tenant may keep bicycles and ordinary personal belongings in designated common areas subject to society rules.
rationale: The clause creates a defined use right subject to objective building rules.

clause_text: Assignment consent shall not be unreasonably withheld where the proposed replacement tenant satisfies agreed eligibility criteria.
rationale: The clause limits arbitrary refusal while preserving landlord screening.

clause_text: Tenant shall not transfer possession through an informal roommate arrangement without updating the agreement.
rationale: The requirement is reasonable but should distinguish ordinary co-occupancy from a transfer of possession.

clause_text: Commercial activity causing customer footfall or material nuisance requires prior written consent.
rationale: The clause focuses on measurable property impact rather than banning all home work.

clause_text: Tenant shall not remove landlord-owned fixtures or appliances from the premises.
rationale: The clause protects owner property.

clause_text: The permitted occupants shall be listed in an annexure, with reasonable updates allowed for family changes.
rationale: A documented occupant list can improve clarity while allowing normal life changes.

clause_text: The parties shall sign the tenancy agreement in writing and each retain a signed copy.
rationale: A written signed agreement provides strong evidence of the agreed terms.

clause_text: The tenant shall receive no copy of the executed agreement until the lease expires.
rationale: Withholding the tenant's copy materially weakens proof of contractual rights.

clause_text: Any amendment to rent, deposit, or termination terms must be recorded in writing and signed by both parties.
rationale: Written amendments reduce disputes over informal changes.

clause_text: The landlord may modify any term by sending a unilateral email without tenant acceptance.
rationale: Unilateral modification of material contractual terms undermines mutual consent.

clause_text: The agreement shall identify the premises, rent, deposit, term, notice rules, and payment method.
rationale: Core commercial terms should be identifiable in the agreement.

clause_text: The tenant shall sign blank annexures that the landlord may complete later.
rationale: Blank signed documents create a serious alteration and fraud risk.

clause_text: A move-in inventory shall be attached and signed by both parties.
rationale: An inventory is useful evidence for condition and deposit disputes.

clause_text: The landlord may alter the inventory after possession without tenant acknowledgment.
rationale: Unilateral post-handover alteration of evidence undermines reliability.

clause_text: For rent of ₹3,500, the agreement shall identify the rent and term while recognizing that DRCA applicability depends on the statutory conditions.
